sentences.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. vs S.Neelaveni And 4
Others on 21 July, 2023

The Hon'Ble Smt Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 C.R.P.No.2590 Of 2019
O R D E R:

Challenging the order dated 29.03.2019 passed in I.A. No. 589 of 2018 in M.V.O.P.No. 2167 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal Cum X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad, the present Civil Revision Petition is filed by the revision petitioner/respondent No.4.
2.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal Cum X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties will be referred as per their array before the trial Court 3.

The facts of the case are that the revision petitioner, Shriram General Insurance Company limited,
who was arrayed as respondent No.4 before the Tribunal, filed an application under Section 5 of limitation Act read with Section 151 of CPC to condone the delay of 704 days in filing the petition to set aside the exparte judgment and decree dated 10.12.2015 passed against it in M.V.O.P.No.2167 of 2011.

According to the revision petitioner, only upon receipt of copy of the said judgment and decree on 16.10.2017, it came to know that the above matter was filed by respondent No.1 and others claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the death of one S.Suresh MGP,J under the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act against respondent No. 1, owner, respondent No. 2, insurer of the offending vehicle i.e., Mini lorry bearing No. AP 28 E 1453.

It is stated that on 10.05.2011, the deceased was proceeding as passenger in Auto bearing No. AP 04 TV 0738 from Miyapur cross roads to Bollaram road and when he reached near kanakadurga temple on the turning of Bollaram road, the Auto fell towards other side of the road by hitting the road divider as one of the tyres of the Auto went flat.
Meanwhile, the offending lorry came in rash and negligent manner and ran over the body of the deceased by hitting the said Auto.
As a result, the deceased succumbed to the injuries in the hospital.

It is further stated that after receipt of notice from this Court in the I.A.No.824 of 2014 as well as impleading petition, the then dealing officer of the revision petitioner, has sent the papers to the Headquarters, Jaipur, Rajasthan State, who is competent authority to entrust the matter to the Panel advocate after registering it in the computer system.

Since they have not received the said papers, they could not enter the details in the system and thereby failed to entrust the matter to the Panel advocate, as such the revision petitioner-Insurance Company was set ex parte and ex parte judgment and decree was passed by Tribunal on 10.12.2015.

As MGP,J the papers are misplaced and the same are not received by the petitioner's head office, they could not represent the matter in time and accordingly an ex parte judgment and decree was passed.
Thus, there is a delay of 704 days in filing the petition to set aside the judgment and decree dated 10.12.2015 which is wanton nor willful but for the reason stated above.

sentences.text: 4. Before the tribunal, the revision petition-respondent No.4 filed counter contending that tribunal has issued notices to the revision petitioner and the same was received by the revision petitioner on 03.09.2014 an only after receiving notice the tribunal passed orders on merits.
Even after receipt of notice, the revision petitioner did not turn up to appear before the tribunal, hence, by order dated 14.09.2015 the revision petitioner was set ex parte.
The reasons assigned by the revision petitioner for condoning the huge delay of 704 days is not convincing and miserably failed to explain day to day.
Hence they are not entitled for relief and prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Considering the counter filed by revision petitioner and both oral and documentary evidence available on record, the tribunal has dismissed the application.
Aggrieved by the same, the revision petitioner filed the present revision.
MGP,J 6.
Heard learned Standing Counsel for the revision petitioner.
Despite service of notice, the learned counsel for the respondents did not turn up to submit arguments.
Perused the material available on record.

7. The main contention of the learned counsel for the revision petitioner is that thought the notice has been received by the Headquarters at Jaipur, Rajasthan, who is the competent authority to entrust the matter to the Panel advocate after registering in the computer system.
However, they have not received the said papers as such they could not entrust the same to the Panel advocate.
Therefore, the revision petitioner was set ex parte and ex parte judgment and decree was passed.
8. It is pertinent to state that the notice will be sent to the Headquarters at Jaipur, Rajasthan and it being the superior authority has to entrust the matter to the Panel advocates.
In the present case, as per the learned counsel for the revision petitioner, they have neither received the material paper nor got informed regarding registration of the cases.
Therefore, they could not entrust the same to the Panel advocates.
Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the revision petitioner has made out a reasonable cause to condone MGP,J delay of 704 days.

Therefore,
in order to give an opportunity to the revision petitioner, the present revision can be allowed by imposing cost.

9. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petition is allowed setting aside the order dated 10.12.2015 passed by the Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal Cum X Additonal Chief Judge, City Civil Court,
Hyderabad, on payment of cost of Rs.3,000/- payable by the revision petitioner to the respondent Nos.1 and 2/claimants within four weeks from the date of receipt of this Order.

Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
